title: Etiquette & language
body:
Shoes come off at the door in traditional restaurants, ryokan-style lodging, and shrine interiors — watch for a raised floor or a shoe rack and follow it. Trains and buses run near-silent: phone calls are avoided and conversation stays low.

Bowing substitutes for handshakes in most transactions — a small nod back is enough for a visitor. English is limited outside central Hakata/Tenjin and major sights, but signage, menus and ticket machines are usually bilingual; the phrase card in the Trip kit covers the handful of situational lines worth having ready.

Yatai carry their own, stricter etiquette — see the Yatai & specialties tab, since it's specific enough to need its own space rather than a line here.
